title: John Chrysostom on Acts 1:1
body: “To many persons this Book is so little known, both it and its author, that they are not even aware that there is such a book in existence. For this reason especially I have taken this narrative for my subject, that I may draw to it such as do not know it, and not let such a treasure as this remain hidden out of sight.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 1
bodyEs: “Para muchas personas este libro es tan poco conocido, tanto él como su autor, que ni siquiera saben que existe tal libro. Por esta razón sobre todo he tomado esta narración como tema, para atraer a ella a los que no la conocen, y no dejar que un tesoro como este permanezca escondido fuera de la vista.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 1:6
body: “When the disciples intend to ask anything, they approach Him together, that by dint of numbers they may abash Him into compliance. They well knew that in what He had said previously, "Of that day knoweth no man" (Matt.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 2
bodyEs: “Cuando los discípulos piensan pedir algo, se acercan a él juntos, para que a fuerza de número lo avergüencen hasta que acceda. Bien sabían que en lo que había dicho antes, «del día y hora nadie sabe» (Mat.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 1:12
body: “Then after the event, he appositely brings in the Prophet, saying, "For it is written in the Book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein" (v.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 3
bodyEs: “Luego, después del suceso, trae con oportunidad al profeta, diciendo: «Porque está escrito en el libro de los salmos: Sea hecha desierta su habitación, y no haya quien more en ella» (v.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 2:1
body: “Dost thou perceive the type? What is this Pentecost? The time when the sickle was to be put to the harvest, and the ingathering was made.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 4
bodyEs: “¿Percibes el tipo? ¿Qué es este Pentecostés? El tiempo en que la hoz había de ponerse a la mies, y se hacía la recolección.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 2:14
body: “Here he directs his discourse to those others, the mockers, and while he seems to reason with those, he sets these right. For indeed it was divinely ordered that "some mocked," that he might have a starting-point for his defence, and by means of that defence, might teach.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 5
bodyEs: “Aquí dirige su discurso a aquellos otros, los burladores, y mientras parece razonar con esos, endereza a estos. Porque en verdad estaba divinamente dispuesto que «algunos se burlaban», para que tuviera un punto de partida para su defensa, y por medio de esa defensa pudiera enseñar.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 2:22
body: “Here again he begins with an introduction, that they may not become excited, now that he is going to make express mention to them of Jesus: for in what preceded, there was no reason why they should be excited, while the Prophet was the subject of discourse: but the name of Jesus would have given offence at the very outset.--And he does not say, "Do as I bid you," but, Hear; as being not at all exacting.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 6
bodyEs: “Aquí otra vez empieza con una introducción, para que no se exciten, ahora que va a mencionarles expresamente a Jesús: porque en lo anterior no había razón para que se excitaran, mientras el profeta era el tema del discurso; pero el nombre de Jesús habría ofendido desde el primer momento. Y no dice: «Hagan como yo les mando», sino: Oigan; como quien no exige nada.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 3:1
body: “Everywhere we find these two Apostles in great harmony together. "To him Simon Peter beckoned." (John xiii.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 8
bodyEs: “En todas partes hallamos a estos dos apóstoles en gran armonía juntos. «A éste, pues, hizo señas Simón Pedro». (Juan 13.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 3:12
body: “There is greater freedom of speech in this harangue, than in the former. Not that he was afraid on the former occasion, but the persons whom he addressed there, being jesters and scoffers, would not have borne it.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 9
bodyEs: “Hay mayor libertad de palabra en este discurso que en el anterior. No es que tuviera miedo en la ocasión anterior, sino que las personas a quienes habló allí, siendo burlones y escarnecedores, no lo habrían soportado.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 4:1
body: “Ere yet they had time to take breath after their first trials, straightway they enter into others. And observe how the events are disposed.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 10
bodyEs: “Aún no habían tenido tiempo de recobrar el aliento después de sus primeras pruebas, y enseguida entran en otras. Y observa cómo están dispuestos los acontecimientos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 4:23
body: “Not for their own glory did they tell the tale--how should such be their motive?--but what they displayed was the proofs therein exhibited of the grace of Christ.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 11
bodyEs: “No por su propia gloria contaron el relato —¿cómo habría de ser ese su motivo?— sino que lo que mostraron fueron las pruebas allí exhibidas de la gracia de Cristo.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 4:36
body: “And Joses, who by the Apostles was surnamed Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation), a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the Apostles' feet.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 12
bodyEs: “«Entonces José, que fué llamado de los apóstoles por sobrenombre, Bernabé, (que es interpretado, Hijo de consolación) Levita, natural de Cipro, como tuviese una heredad, la vendió, y trajo el precio, y púsolo á los pies de los apóstoles».”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 5:17
body: “But it is necessary now to look over again what we have read. "But the angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them forth, and said, Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 13
bodyEs: “Pero es necesario ahora volver a mirar lo que hemos leído. «Mas el ángel del Señor, abriendo de noche las puertas de la cárcel, y sacándolos, dijo: Id, y estando en el templo, hablad al pueblo todas las palabras de esta vida».”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 5:34
body: “This Gamaliel was Paul's teacher. And one may well wonder, how, being so right-minded in his judgment, and withal learned in the law, he did not yet believe.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 14
bodyEs: “Este Gamaliel era el maestro de Pablo. Y bien puede uno maravillarse de cómo, siendo tan recto en su juicio, y además docto en la ley, todavía no creía.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 6:8
body: “See how even among the seven one was preëminent, and won the first prize. For though the ordination was common to him and them, yet he drew upon himself greater grace.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 15
bodyEs: “Mira cómo aun entre los siete uno sobresalía, y ganó el primer premio. Porque aunque la ordenación era común a él y a ellos, él atrajo sobre sí una gracia mayor.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 7:6
body: “See, what a number of years the Promise has been given, and the manner of the Promise, and nowhere sacrifice, nowhere circumcision! He here shows, how God Himself suffered them to be afflicted, not that He had anything to lay to their charge.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 16
bodyEs: “Mira cuántos años hace que se ha dado la Promesa, y la manera de la Promesa, ¡y en ninguna parte sacrificio, en ninguna parte circuncisión! Aquí muestra cómo Dios mismo permitió que fueran afligidos, no porque tuviera algo que echarles en cara.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 7:35
body: “This is very suitable to the matter in hand. "This Moses," he says. "This," the man who had been in danger of losing his life; the man who had been set at naught by them; "this" the man whom they had declined: "this" same, God having raised up, sent unto them.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 17
bodyEs: “Esto viene muy bien al asunto. «Este Moisés», dice. «Este», el hombre que había estado en peligro de perder la vida; el hombre que había sido despreciado por ellos; «este», el hombre a quien habían rechazado: a «este» mismo, habiéndolo levantado Dios, lo envió a ellos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 7:54
body: “See, once more, the wrong-doers in trouble. Just as the Jews are perplexed, saying, "What are we to do with these men?" so these also are "cut to the heart." (ch.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 18
bodyEs: “Mira, una vez más, a los malhechores en apuros. Así como los judíos están perplejos, diciendo: «¿Qué hemos de hacer á estos hombres?», así también estos «regañaban de sus corazones». (cap.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 8:26
body: “It seems to me, this (Philip) was one of the seven; for from Jerusalem he would not have gone southwards, but to the north; but from Samaria it was "towards the south. The same is desert:" so that there is no fear of an attack from the Jews.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 19
bodyEs: “Me parece que este (Felipe) era uno de los siete; porque desde Jerusalén no habría ido hacia el sur, sino hacia el norte; pero desde Samaria era «hacia el sur. Este es desierto»: de modo que no hay temor de un ataque de los judíos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 9:10
body: “What may be the reason that He neither drew any one of high authority and importance, nor caused such to be forthcoming for the purpose of instructing Paul? It was, because it was not meet that he should be induced by men, but only by Christ Himself: as in fact this man taught him nothing, but merely baptized him; for, as soon as baptized (photistheis), he was to draw upon himself the grace of the Spirit, by his zeal and exceeding earnestness.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 20
bodyEs: “¿Cuál puede ser la razón de que no atrajera a nadie de alta autoridad e importancia, ni hiciera que tal persona se presentara para instruir a Pablo? Fue porque no convenía que lo indujeran los hombres, sino solo Cristo mismo: pues de hecho este hombre no le enseñó nada, sino que solo lo bautizó; porque, apenas bautizado (photistheis), había de atraer sobre sí la gracia del Espíritu, por su celo y su fervor extraordinario.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 9:26
body: “One may well be much at a loss here to understand how it is that, whereas in the Epistle to the Galatians Paul says, "I went not to Jerusalem," but "into Arabia" and "to Damascus," and, "After three years I went up to Jerusalem," and "to see Peter" (Gal.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 21
bodyEs: “Bien puede uno quedar muy perplejo aquí para entender cómo es que, mientras en la Epístola a los Gálatas Pablo dice: «Ni fuí á Jerusalem», sino «á la Arabia» y «á Damasco», y «Después, pasados tres años, fuí á Jerusalem» y «á ver á Pedro» (Gál.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 10:1
body: “This man is not a Jew, nor of those under the Law, but he had already forestalled our manner of life. Observe, thus far, two persons, both of high rank, receiving the faith, the eunuch at Gaza and this man; and the pains taken on behalf of these men.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 22
bodyEs: “Este hombre no es judío, ni de los que están bajo la Ley, sino que ya se había adelantado a nuestro modo de vida. Observa, hasta aquí, a dos personas, ambas de alto rango, que reciben la fe: el eunuco en Gaza y este hombre; y los cuidados tomados en favor de estos hombres.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 10:44
body: “Observe God's providential management. He does not suffer the speech to be finished, nor the baptism to take place upon a command of Peter, but, when He has made it evident how admirable their state of mind is, and a beginning is made of the work of teaching, and they have believed that assuredly baptism is the remission of sins, then forthwith comes the Spirit upon them.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 24
bodyEs: “Observa el manejo providencial de Dios. No permite que el discurso se termine, ni que el bautismo se haga por un mandato de Pedro, sino que, cuando ha dejado en claro cuán admirable es su estado de ánimo, y se ha empezado la obra de la enseñanza, y han creído que ciertamente el bautismo es el perdón de los pecados, entonces enseguida viene el Espíritu sobre ellos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 11:19
body: “The persecution turned out to be no slight benefit as "to them that love God all things work together for good." (Rom.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 25
bodyEs: “La persecución resultó no ser un beneficio pequeño, pues «á los que á Dios aman, todas las cosas les ayudan á bien». (Rom.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 12:1
body: “This is what Christ said: "My cup indeed ye shall drink, and with the baptism wherewith I am baptized, shall ye be baptized." (Mark x.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 26
bodyEs: “Esto es lo que dijo Cristo: «del vaso que yo bebo, beberéis; y del bautismo de que yo soy bautizado, seréis bautizados». (Marcos 10.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 12:18
body: “Some persons, it is likely, are at a loss how to explain it, that God should quietly look on while (His) champions are put to death, and now again the soldiers on account of Peter: and yet it was possible for Him after (delivering) Peter to rescue them also. But it was not yet the time of judgment, so as to render to each according to his deserts.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 27
bodyEs: “Algunas personas, es probable, no saben cómo explicarlo: que Dios mire en silencio mientras matan a (sus) campeones, y ahora otra vez a los soldados por causa de Pedro; y sin embargo le era posible, después de (librar) a Pedro, rescatarlos también a ellos. Pero todavía no era el tiempo del juicio, como para dar a cada uno según sus merecimientos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 13:4
body: “As soon as they were ordained they went forth, and hasted to Cyprus, that being a place where was no ill-design hatching against them, and where moreover the Word had been sown already. In Antioch there were (teachers) enough, and Phoenice too was near to Palestine; but Cyprus not so.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 28
bodyEs: “Apenas fueron ordenados, salieron, y se apresuraron a Chipre, por ser un lugar donde no se tramaba ningún mal designio contra ellos, y donde además la Palabra ya había sido sembrada. En Antioquía había (maestros) suficientes, y Fenicia también estaba cerca de Palestina; pero Chipre no.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 13:16
body: “Behold Barnabas giving place to Paul--how should it be otherwise?--to him whom he brought from Tarsus; just as we find John on all occasions giving way to Peter: and yet Barnabas was more looked up to than Paul: true, but they had an eye only to the common advantage.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 29
bodyEs: “Mira a Bernabé cediendo el lugar a Pablo —¿cómo habría de ser de otro modo?— a aquel a quien él trajo de Tarso; así como hallamos a Juan cediendo en todas las ocasiones a Pedro: y sin embargo a Bernabé se lo miraba más que a Pablo; cierto, pero ellos solo tenían ojo para la ventaja común.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 14:14
body: “Mark the vehemence with which all this is done by the Apostles: "rent their clothes, ran in, cried out," all from strong affection of the soul, revolted by the things that were done. For it was a grief, indeed a grief inconsolable, that they should needs be thought gods, and introduce idolatry, the very thing which they came to destroy!”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 31
bodyEs: “Mira la vehemencia con que los apóstoles hacen todo esto: «rasgaron sus vestidos, corrieron adentro, gritaron», todo por un fuerte afecto del alma, sublevada por las cosas que se hacían. Porque era un dolor, sí, un dolor inconsolable, que tuvieran que ser tenidos por dioses, e introducir la idolatría, precisamente lo que venían a destruir.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 15:1
body: “Mark how at every step of the right progress in respect of the Gentiles, the beginning is brought in as matter of necessity. Before this (Peter) being found fault with, justified himself, and said all that he said in the tone of apology, which was what made his words acceptable: then, the Jews having turned away, upon this (Paul) came to the Gentiles.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 32
bodyEs: “Mira cómo, en cada paso del recto avance respecto de los gentiles, el principio se introduce como materia de necesidad. Antes de esto, (Pedro), al ser reprendido, se justificó, y dijo todo lo que dijo en tono de disculpa, lo cual fue lo que hizo aceptables sus palabras; luego, habiéndose apartado los judíos, sobre esto (Pablo) vino a los gentiles.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 15:13
body: “This (James) was bishop, as they say, and therefore he speaks last, and herein is fulfilled that saying, "In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established." (Deut.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 33
bodyEs: “Este (Santiago) era obispo, según dicen, y por eso habla al final, y en esto se cumple aquel dicho: «En el dicho de dos testigos, ó en el dicho de tres testigos consistirá el negocio». (Deut.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 15:35
body: “Observe again their humility, how they let others also take part in the preaching. "And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 34
bodyEs: “Observa otra vez su humildad, cómo dejan que otros también tomen parte en la predicación. «Y después de algunos días, Pablo dijo á Bernabé: Volvamos á visitar á los hermanos por todas las ciudades en las cuales hemos anunciado la palabra del Señor, cómo están».”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 16:13
body: “See again Paul judaizing. "Where it was thought," it says, both from the time and from the place, "that prayer would be.--Out of the city, by a river side:" for it is not to be supposed that they prayed only where there was a synagogue; they also prayed out of synagogue, but then for this purpose they set apart, as it were, a certain place, because as Jews they were more corporeal--and, "on the sabbath-day," when it was likely that a multitude would come together.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 35
bodyEs: “Mira otra vez a Pablo judaizando. «Donde se pensaba», dice, tanto por el tiempo como por el lugar, «que habría oración. Fuera de la ciudad, junto a un río»: porque no hay que suponer que oraban solo donde había sinagoga; también oraban fuera de la sinagoga, pero entonces, para este propósito, apartaban, por así decir, cierto lugar, porque como judíos eran más corporales; y «en el día de sábado», cuando era probable que se juntara una multitud.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 16:25
body: “What could equal these souls? These men had been scourged, had received many stripes, they had been misused, were in peril of their lives, were thrust into the inner prison, and set fast in the stocks: and for all this they did not suffer themselves to sleep, but kept vigil all the night.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 36
bodyEs: “¿Qué podría igualar a estas almas? Estos hombres habían sido azotados, habían recibido muchos golpes, habían sido maltratados, estaban en peligro de sus vidas, fueron metidos en la cárcel más interior y sujetados en el cepo; y con todo esto no se permitieron dormir, sino que velaron toda la noche.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 17:1
body: “Again they haste past the small cities, and press on to the greater ones, since from those the word was to flow as from a fountain into the neighboring cities. "And Paul, as his manner was, went into the synagogue of the Jews." Although he had said, "We turn to the Gentiles" (ch.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 37
bodyEs: “Otra vez pasan de prisa las ciudades pequeñas y se apresuran a las mayores, pues desde esas la palabra había de fluir como de una fuente a las ciudades vecinas. «Y Pablo, según su costumbre, entró en la sinagoga de los judíos». Aunque había dicho: «nos volvemos á los Gentiles» (cap.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 17:16
body: “Observe how he meets with greater trials among the Jews than among the Gentiles. Thus in Athens he undergoes nothing of this kind; the thing goes as far as ridicule, and there an end: and yet he did make some converts: whereas among the Jews he underwent many perils; so much greater was their hostility against him.--"His spirit," it says, "was roused within him when he saw the city all full of idols." Nowhere else were so many objects of worship to be seen.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 38
bodyEs: “Observa cómo encuentra pruebas mayores entre los judíos que entre los gentiles. Así en Atenas no padece nada de esta clase; la cosa llega hasta la burla, y allí se acaba; y sin embargo sí hizo algunos convertidos; mientras que entre los judíos padeció muchos peligros; tanto mayor era su hostilidad contra él. «Su espíritu», dice, «se enardecía dentro de él al ver la ciudad llena de ídolos». En ninguna otra parte se veían tantos objetos de culto.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 17:32
body: “What can be the reason that, having persuaded (some so far as to say) that they would hear him again, and there being no dangers, Paul is so in haste to leave Athens? Probably he knew that he should do them no great good; moreover he was led by the Spirit to Corinth.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 39
bodyEs: “¿Cuál puede ser la razón de que, habiendo persuadido (a algunos hasta decir) que lo oirían otra vez, y no habiendo peligros, Pablo tenga tanta prisa por dejar Atenas? Probablemente sabía que no les haría gran bien; además, el Espíritu lo llevaba a Corinto.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 18:18
body: “See how the Law was breaking up; see how they were bound by conscience. This, namely, was a Jewish custom, to shear their heads agreeably with a vow.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 40
bodyEs: “Mira cómo la Ley se iba deshaciendo; mira cómo estaban atados por la conciencia. Esto, a saber, era una costumbre judía: cortarse el cabello conforme a un voto.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 19:21
body: “He sends Timothy and Erastus into Macedonia, but himself remains at Ephesus. Having made a long enough stay in that city, he wishes to remove elsewhere again.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 42
bodyEs: “Envía a Timoteo y a Erasto a Macedonia, pero él se queda en Éfeso. Habiendo hecho una estancia ya bastante larga en aquella ciudad, desea trasladarse otra vez a otra parte.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 20:1
body: “There was need of much comforting after that uproar. Accordingly, having done this, he goes into Macedonia, and then into Greece.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 43
bodyEs: “Había necesidad de mucho consuelo después de aquel alboroto. Así, habiendo hecho esto, va a Macedonia, y luego a Grecia.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 20:17
body: “See him, hasting to sail by, and yet not overlooking them, but taking order for all. Having sent for the rulers, through those he discourses to them (the Ephesians): but it is worthy of admiration, how finding himself under a necessity of saying certain great things about himself, he tries to make the least he can of it (peirhata metriazein).”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 44
bodyEs: “Míralo, con prisa de pasar de largo en el barco, y sin embargo sin pasarlos por alto, sino poniendo orden en todo. Habiendo mandado llamar a los gobernantes, por medio de ellos discurre con ellos (los efesios); pero es digno de admiración cómo, hallándose en la necesidad de decir ciertas cosas grandes acerca de sí mismo, procura reducirlas al mínimo (peirhata metriazein).”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 20:32
body: “What he does when writing in an Epistle, this he does also when speaking in council: from exhorting, he ends with prayer: for since he had much alarmed them by saying, "Grievous wolves shall enter in among you" (v.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 45
bodyEs: “Lo que hace cuando escribe en una epístola, esto hace también cuando habla en el concilio: de la exhortación pasa a la oración; porque, como los había alarmado mucho al decir: «entrarán en medio de vosotros lobos rapaces» (v.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 21:18
body: “This was the Bishop of Jerusalem; and to him (Paul) is sent on an earlier occasion. This (James) was brother of the Lord; a great and admirable man.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 46
bodyEs: “Este era el obispo de Jerusalén; y a él (Pablo) es enviado en una ocasión anterior. Este (Santiago) era hermano del Señor; un hombre grande y admirable.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 21:39
body: “Observe how, when he discourses to those that are without, he does not decline availing himself of the aids afforded by the laws. Here he awes the tribune by the name of his city.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 47
bodyEs: “Observa cómo, cuando discurre con los de afuera, no rehuye valerse de las ayudas que ofrecen las leyes. Aquí impone respeto al tribuno con el nombre de su ciudad.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 22:17
body: “See how he thrusts himself (into danger), I came, he says, after that vision, "to Jerusalem. I was in a trance," etc.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 48
bodyEs: “Mira cómo se mete él mismo (en el peligro). Vine, dice, después de aquella visión, «a Jerusalén. Estaba en éxtasis», etc.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 23:31
body: “Like some king whom his body-guards escort, so did these convey Paul; in such numbers too, and by night, for fear of the wrath of the people. Now then you will say that they have got him out of the city, they desist from their violence?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 50
bodyEs: “Como a un rey al que escoltan sus guardias, así lo llevaban estos a Pablo; y en tal número, y de noche, por miedo a la ira del pueblo. Ahora bien, dirás que, una vez que lo han sacado de la ciudad, ¿cesan de su violencia?”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 24:22
body: “See how much close investigation is made by the many in a long course of time, that it should not be said that the trial was hurried over. For, as the orator had made mention of Lysias, that he took "him away with violence, Felix," he says, "deferred them.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 51
bodyEs: “Mira cuánta investigación minuciosa hacen los muchos en un largo curso de tiempo, para que no se diga que el juicio se precipitó. Porque, como el orador había mencionado a Lisias, que se lo «llevó con violencia, Félix», dice, «los difirió».”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 25:23
body: “See what an audience is gathered together for Paul. Having collected all his guards, the governor is come, and the king, and the tribunes, "with the principal men," it says, "of the city." Then Paul being brought forth, see how he is proclaimed as conqueror.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 52
bodyEs: “Mira qué auditorio se reúne para Pablo. Habiendo reunido a todos sus guardias, viene el gobernador, y el rey, y los tribunos, «con los principales», dice, «de la ciudad». Luego, sacado Pablo, mira cómo se lo proclama como vencedor.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 26:30
body: “See how again also they pass sentence in his favor, and after having said, "Thou art beside thyself," (v.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 53
bodyEs: “Mira cómo otra vez también dictan sentencia a su favor, y después de haber dicho: «Estás loco» (v.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 28:1
body: “And they do not assail him forthwith, but for a time respect him on account of his misfortune: nor do they openly proclaim their surmise, but speak it "among themselves: a murderer;" for the bonds led them to suspect this. "They showed no small kindness," and yet (some of them) were prisoners.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 54
bodyEs: “Y no lo acometen enseguida, sino que por un tiempo lo respetan a causa de su desgracia; ni proclaman abiertamente su sospecha, sino que la hablan «entre sí: un homicida»; porque las cadenas los llevaban a sospechar esto. «Mostraron no poca bondad», y sin embargo (algunos de ellos) eran presos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Acts 28:17
body: “He wished to exculpate both himself and others; himself, that they might not accuse him, and by so doing hurt themselves; and those (others), that it might not seem that the whole thing was of their doing. For it was likely that a report was prevalent, that he had been delivered up by the Jews; and this was enough to alarm them.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans, Homily 55
bodyEs: “Quería disculpar tanto a sí mismo como a otros; a sí mismo, para que no lo acusaran y, al hacerlo, se hicieran daño; y a aquellos (otros), para que no pareciera que todo el asunto era obra de ellos. Porque era probable que corriera un rumor de que había sido entregado por los judíos; y esto bastaba para alarmarlos.”
